nodes.label: Wiki Export (--wiki)
nodes.rationale: Must run before Step 9 cleanup so .graphify_labels.json is still available; only runs when --wiki was explicitly given.

nodes.label: Neo4j Cypher Export
nodes.rationale: Two modes: --neo4j writes a Cypher file for manual import via cypher-shell, --neo4j-push writes directly over bolt://. Uses MERGE so re-running never duplicates.

nodes.label: FalkorDB Export
nodes.rationale: The file export is discouraged because FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time with no bulk script import; --falkordb-push is preferred and the file form kept only as a portable cypher.txt artifact.

nodes.label: MERGE-Based Idempotent Graph Import
nodes.rationale: Both graph-database exports emit MERGE rather than CREATE so a repeated push is safe and does not accumulate duplicate nodes.

nodes.label: Graphify stdio MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats and shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live. Claude Desktop config must use the absolute interpreter path from .graphify_python because Claude Desktop cannot run $(...) and the system python3 cannot import graphify under uv tool install.

nodes.label: Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Gated on total_words > 5000 because for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression, so the benchmark would be misleading.

nodes.label: Graphify Extraction Subagent Prompt
nodes.rationale: Loaded only in Step 3 Part B when the corpus has at least one doc, paper or image chunk; a pure-code corpus skips semantic extraction entirely because AST already covers it.

nodes.label: Discrete Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: Five fixed values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) replace a continuous range because models follow discrete rubrics better; production showed a bimodal collapse with >50% of edges at 0.5 and >40% at 0.85+, i.e. the range was being treated as binary. If no value fits, mark AMBIGUOUS rather than emitting <=0.4.

nodes.label: Full-Path Node ID Format
nodes.rationale: IDs keep every directory level so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and the ID matches what the AST extractor generates; filename-only or immediate-parent IDs create orphan ghost-duplicate nodes. IDs must be deterministic from the label alone, never suffixed with chunk numbers, so the same entity resolves identically across chunks.

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file Rule
nodes.rationale: Paths are copied character-for-character from FILE_LIST so the full build and incremental --update share one base; the engine relativizes downstream, and build_merge's replace-on-re-extract then matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.

nodes.label: Six-Value file_type Enum
nodes.rationale: Exactly code, document, paper, image, rationale, concept; any other value is rejected. Rationale is stored as an attribute on a real concept node rather than as its own node, so the graph holds named entities only.

nodes.label: Cross-Language Call Edge Prohibition
nodes.rationale: A calls edge must stay inside one language and point caller -> callee; a Python function cannot call a JS/TS/Go/Rust/Java symbol, so such edges are phantom artifacts.

nodes.label: Semantic Similarity Edges
nodes.rationale: Captures concepts that solve the same problem with no import, call or citation linking them; reserved for genuinely non-obvious cross-cutting similarity so the graph is not flooded with trivial matches.

nodes.label: Hyperedges
nodes.rationale: Group three or more nodes into one shared concept, flow or pattern that pairwise edges cannot express; capped at three per chunk to keep them informative.

nodes.label: DEEP_MODE Aggressive Inference
nodes.rationale: --mode deep asks for indirect deps, shared assumptions and latent couplings, preferring an AMBIGUOUS mark over omission.

nodes.label: graphify clone
nodes.rationale: Clones into ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo> and reuses an existing clone on repeat runs, so re-running the skill does not re-download.

nodes.label: Cross-Repo Graph Merge (merge-graphs)
nodes.rationale: Each repo is built independently and merged afterwards; every node carries a repo attribute so the merged graph can be filtered by origin.

nodes.label: Per-Subfolder Monorepo Extraction
nodes.rationale: The skill pipeline always writes graphify-out/ into the current working directory, so running it per subfolder clobbers the same output dir; the CLI is used directly instead because graphify extract places graphify-out/ inside the scanned path, and the parts are merged at the project root.

nodes.label: Graphify Post-Commit Hook
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a background watcher because it fires once per commit and works with any editor; it diffs HEAD~1, re-runs AST extraction on changed code files and rebuilds graph.json and GRAPH_REPORT.md. Doc and image changes are deliberately ignored (they need an LLM pass) and an existing hook is appended to rather than replaced.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration (graphify claude install)
nodes.rationale: Writes a ## graphify section into the project's local CLAUDE.md so the graph is consulted before answering codebase questions without the user typing /graphify each session.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: The query CLI matches labels by case-folded substring plus IDF with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language matching, so a question phrased in different vocabulary returns zero hits and the answer collapses to noise. The fix is to dump the graph's actual label vocabulary to .vocab.txt and let the model pick up to 12 tokens from that exact list, never inventing tokens; if nothing matches, say so and stop rather than fabricating a search. The selection is printed so the expansion is auditable.

nodes.label: BFS Traversal Mode
nodes.rationale: Default mode, depth 3, best for 'what is X connected to' - broad context with nearest neighbors first.

nodes.label: DFS Traversal Mode
nodes.rationale: Selected with --dfs for 'how does X reach Y' chain tracing; depth-limited to 6 so it does not traverse the whole graph.

nodes.label: Token-Budget-Aware Subgraph Output
nodes.rationale: Nodes are ranked by term overlap and the rendering is truncated at roughly 4 chars per token against a default 2000-token budget, so the most relevant part of the subgraph survives the cut.

nodes.label: Answer Only From The Graph
nodes.rationale: Answers must use only what the subgraph contains, quoting source_location as a citation; if the graph lacks the information, say so rather than hallucinating edges.

nodes.label: save-result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Writes the verbatim question, the answer (including the expanded-token trace) and the cited nodes back so the next --update extracts the Q&A as a graph node, closing the loop and improving future queries.

nodes.label: Work Memory and LESSONS.md Reflection
nodes.rationale: An --outcome of useful, dead_end or corrected turns saved answers into preferred sources, known dead ends and corrections. graphify reflect --if-stale is deterministic and LLM-free, so a session-start refresh is nearly free and stays current even without the post-commit hook.

nodes.label: /graphify path (Shortest Path)
nodes.rationale: Finds the shortest path between two named concepts via nx.shortest_path and then explains each hop in plain language.

nodes.label: /graphify explain (Single Node)
nodes.rationale: Dumps one node's source, type, degree and every neighbor with relation and confidence, then asks for a 3-5 sentence plain-language explanation citing source locations.

nodes.label: Whisper Video/Audio Transcription Step
nodes.rationale: Video and audio cannot be read directly, so they are transcribed to text and then treated as ordinary doc files in Step 3B. The transcript JSON is written from Python rather than by a shell redirect because Whisper prints progress to stdout and would corrupt the file (#1392). A failed file logs a warning and the run continues.

nodes.label: Self-Authored Whisper Domain Hint
nodes.rationale: The agent reads god-node labels from .graphify_detect.json and writes the one-sentence domain hint itself, so no extra API call is needed; a corpus of only video falls back to a generic punctuation prompt. GRAPHIFY_WHISPER_PROMPT and GRAPHIFY_WHISPER_MODEL must be exported so the child Python process sees them.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts only changed files to save tokens and time. .graphify_detect.json is rewritten so files carries the changed subset that drives AST and cache steps while all_files carries the full corpus for steps needing corpus-wide context. A deletions-only run still writes an empty extraction so the merge can prune.

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-on-Re-Extract
nodes.rationale: build_merge reads graph.json directly with no NetworkX round-trip so edge direction is preserved (#801). prune_sources is only for genuinely deleted files: changed files are reconciled by replace-on-re-extract (#1344), and adding them to prune would delete the fresh content. root= must be passed so absolute prune paths relativize against the graph's relative source_file values, otherwise stale nodes accumulate every update (#1361). directed must be threaded through or a --directed --update silently rebuilds undirected and collapses reciprocal edges (#1392). Hyperedges are taken from the merged graph so prior-run hyperedges are not dropped.

nodes.label: Code-Only Change Fast Path
nodes.rationale: If every changed file has a code extension, only AST extraction runs and semantic subagents are skipped entirely - no LLM cost. If any changed file is a doc, paper, image or video the full pipeline runs, and changed videos must be transcribed and moved into files['document'] first so raw .mp4/.mp3 paths are never handed to a semantic subagent as unreadable media (#1392).

nodes.label: Selective Semantic Manifest Stamping
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output this run are stamped, so a changed doc whose chunk failed stays unstamped and is re-queued instead of being marked done and lost forever (#2015); dispatched-but-unstamped files have their stale semantic_hash cleared (#1948). Manifest keys stay relative to the scan root so they survive clones and moves (#1417), and scan_corpus is the raw full corpus so newly excluded in-root files are dropped rather than looking like deletions (#1908).

nodes.label: Post-Update Graph Diff
nodes.rationale: graph.json is copied to .graphify_old.json before the merge so graph_diff can report new nodes and edges afterwards; the backup is deleted once shown.

nodes.label: Cluster-Only Rebuild (--cluster-only)
nodes.rationale: graphify cluster-only is self-contained: it re-clusters, names communities and regenerates GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.json and graph.html. Steps 5-9 must not be re-run because they read intermediate files a prior build's cleanup already deleted and would raise FileNotFoundError (#1392).

nodes.label: Refactor Safely Skill (Claude)
nodes.rationale: Refactoring is always previewed before it is applied - rename mode returns an edit list, and impact radius plus affected flows are checked first so no critical path is silently broken.

nodes.label: Graph Tool Token Efficiency Rules
nodes.rationale: Shared footer across every graph skill: start with get_minimal_context_tool, use detail_level=minimal and escalate only when insufficient, target <=5 tool calls and <=800 output tokens, and always read the implementation and its tests before changing code because the graph narrows scope but does not replace the source.

nodes.label: Review Changes Skill (Claude)
nodes.rationale: Review sequence is risk-scored change detection, affected flows, per-function test coverage, then blast radius; findings are grouped by risk level and end in a merge recommendation.

nodes.label: Debug Issue Skill (CodeBuddy)
nodes.rationale: Traces an issue by semantic search, then callers_of/callees_of chains, then full flows; recent changes are checked because they are the most common source of new issues.

nodes.label: Explore Codebase Skill (CodeBuddy)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately broad-to-narrow: stats and architecture overview first, then communities, then specific symbols and relationship traces.

nodes.label: Refactor Safely Skill (CodeBuddy)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical copy of the Claude-scoped refactor-safely skill, duplicated per IDE agent directory.

nodes.label: Review Changes Skill (CodeBuddy)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical copy of the Claude-scoped review-changes skill, duplicated per IDE agent directory.

nodes.label: Debug Issue Skill (Gemini)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical copy of the CodeBuddy debug-issue skill, duplicated per IDE agent directory.

nodes.label: Explore Codebase Skill (Gemini)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical copy of the CodeBuddy explore-codebase skill, duplicated per IDE agent directory.

nodes.label: Refactor Safely Skill (Gemini)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical copy of the Claude-scoped refactor-safely skill, duplicated per IDE agent directory.

nodes.label: Review Changes Skill (Gemini)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical copy of the Claude-scoped review-changes skill, duplicated per IDE agent directory.

nodes.label: code-review-graph MCP Tools Directive (Copilot)
nodes.rationale: applyTo '**' so every file in the repo picks up the instruction to start from the graph for token-efficient exploration and review. Condensed variant of the same block that lives in CLAUDE.md and .kiro/steering.

nodes.label: Graph-First, Verify-In-Source Principle
nodes.rationale: The graph is cheaper than scanning files and supplies callers, dependents and test coverage that file search cannot, but it may be stale or may not model a relationship - so it narrows scope only. When graph and source disagree the source wins, and an empty result means 'not indexed' or 'not statically visible', not 'does not exist'. Behavior, database logic, migrations, retries, fallbacks, recovery and compatibility code must be verified in the exact source.

nodes.label: code-review-graph MCP Tools Steering (Kiro)
nodes.rationale: Kiro steering copy of the same graph-first directive, delimited by code-review-graph MCP tools HTML comment markers so the installer can update it in place.

nodes.label: Graph Auto-Update Review Workflow
nodes.rationale: The graph auto-updates on file changes via hooks, so the review loop is detect_changes_tool, then get_affected_flows_tool for impact, then query_graph_tool pattern=tests_for for coverage.

nodes.label: Field Supervisor Conversation Screen (AI Asking Date)
nodes.rationale: Mobile mockup fixed at 390px and centered, modelling the moment NAVIS detects a missing field in a free-text progress report ('spool erection on the 24 inch header is done') and asks a single targeted clarification. Supervisor turns are right-aligned on plain surface; assistant turns are left-aligned on primary-fixed, so authorship is readable at a glance on a construction site.

nodes.label: Date Clarification Prompt
nodes.rationale: 'Which date was it completed?' - one question per turn rather than a form, because the supervisor is answering hands-free and a single slot is the most that can be held in a voice turn.

nodes.label: Voice-First Input Area with Text Fallback
nodes.rationale: A full-width primary 'Answer by Voice' button is the dominant affordance with a 'Type your answer' field directly beneath it, so a noisy site or a failed recognition never blocks data capture. Pinned above the bottom nav in a fixed panel so it is reachable without scrolling the transcript.

nodes.label: Animated Speaking Waveform Indicator
nodes.rationale: Five CSS-animated staggered bars plus the label 'NAVIS Assistant is speaking' give turn-taking feedback without audio, paired with a replay button so a missed question can be repeated instead of guessed at.

nodes.label: Bottom Navigation with Clarifications Tab
nodes.rationale: Four tabs - Home, Reports, Clarifications, Profile - with Clarifications shown active and filled, making pending ambiguity a first-class destination in the app rather than a transient dialog.

nodes.label: NAVIS Material 3 Tailwind Token Theme
nodes.rationale: Inline tailwind.config declaring a Material 3 role palette (primary #003f87, surface/on-surface, tertiary, error, container tiers), class-based dark mode, an Inter type scale (display-lg through label-md) and named spacing units (stack-sm/md/lg, gutter, container-padding) so every mockup renders from the same tokens without a build step.

nodes.label: Data Entry Session Screen (AI Asking Quantity)
nodes.rationale: Later state of the same clarification dialogue, labelled 'DATA ENTRY SESSION' and framed as a dismissible modal task (close and overflow buttons instead of a bottom nav), signalling a bounded session the supervisor completes and exits rather than a persistent tab.

nodes.label: Quantity Clarification Prompt
nodes.rationale: 'How many were completed out of the planned quantity?' asked only after the date slot was filled ('yesterday'), and rendered on solid primary rather than the muted container used for answered turns so the one open question is visually unmistakable.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Slot-Filling Transcript
nodes.rationale: Four alternating turns (report, date question, 'yesterday', quantity question) stay on screen with tail-notched bubbles and a smart_toy icon on assistant turns, so the supervisor can audit which fields have already been captured before answering the next one.
